specification.title: Cloud ASN membership is contextual, not benignness evidence
specification.description: Membership in a known cloud/hosting ASN is contextual and must not independently establish BENIGN; with no other evidence the acceptable envelope is INCONCLUSIVE.
specification.purpose: Verify the analyst treats membership in a known cloud/hosting ASN as contextual-only and never as independent evidence for a BENIGN verdict.
specification.operational_relevance: Threat triage routinely sees targets that merely share hosting-provider infrastructure; treating cloud-ASN membership as a benign signal would clear malicious infrastructure shared with unrelated tenants.
specification.regression_risk: The analyst could weight ASN co-location as positive reputation, emit a BENIGN verdict, or promote the context evidence into a material finding.

required: The Assessment verdict is INCONCLUSIVE with low or medium confidence when only cloud-ASN context exists
The Assessment states the cloud-ASN contextual limitation
forbidden: No Supporting finding cites the cloud-ASN context evidence
The Assessment reaches a BENIGN verdict

fixture.objective: Assess whether cloud ASN ownership indicates anything about the target IP's maliciousness.

required_limitations: Hosting in a cloud ASN does not establish benignity.
